sourceHtml:
Developers increasingly use Codex with Amazon Bedrock to explore unfamiliar code, make changes, and handle repetitive engineering work. For platform teams, the challenge is to make those tools available without creating a second model-access, identity, and operations stack.

Codex can use Amazon Bedrock for inference with supported OpenAI models. In this post, we show how to fit that path into the AWS identity, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), Regional, and observability practices your organization already uses. Codex still runs on the developer workstation. The main design choice is how its model requests reach Amazon Bedrock and where your organization applies policy and operational controls.

We begin with a small, least-privilege pilot and work through the checks that matter before access expands. The examples use GPT-5.6 Sol. Before starting the pilot, review Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock to confirm that Sol, Terra, or Luna is available in the AWS Region and inference path you plan to use.

Recommended default: Start with Native AWS Access for a small, least-privilege pilot. Choose AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, when you want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Choose an LLM Gateway when a platform team wants to enforce controls in the request path. A custom integration is the advanced version of the LLM Gateway pattern, not a quick start.

The examples come from the open source Guidance for Codex on AWS repository. It includes quick starts for Native AWS Access, AgentCore Gateway, LiteLLM on ECS, Portkey, the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT), and the Amazon CloudWatch setup used later in the post. Choose the quick start that matches your architecture, use it for the pilot, and adapt it to your environment.

Choose your rollout path

Authentication is only one part of an enterprise rollout. Decide who can use the service and which models and Regions are approved. Also define where configuration lives, what telemetry to collect, how usage is allocated, and which skills or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers are allowed. The following table maps those needs to an access path and an owning team.

Choose the access path that provides the controls you need now. The most straightforward path that meets the requirement usually has the lowest operational overhead.

Decision rules

  1. Native AWS Access is the usual starting point when AWS identity and IAM controls are enough for the pilot.
  2. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Within the platform, AgentCore Gateway fits teams that want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for routing, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, or related controls.
  3. A large language model (LLM) Gateway fits organizations that already operate a gateway or want to enforce controls in the request path. Building a custom gateway is the advanced version of this option.

The following diagram compares where identity, routing, policy, telemetry, and operational ownership sit across the three rollout paths.

Figure 1: Codex runs on the developer workstation in each scenario. Native AWS Access uses AWS IAM Identity Center, a configured AgentCore Gateway can apply managed routing and Guardrails, and a configured LLM Gateway can apply request-path controls

Native AWS Access

If Native AWS Access fits the pilot, the repository’s Native AWS Access quick start provides the complete procedure and supporting files. The following abbreviated walkthrough focuses on the sequence and the checks that matter most.

Use your workforce identity provider for sign-in

Employees continue to sign in through the identity provider they already use. In this example, Okta handles authentication through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and provisions users and groups into IAM Identity Center through System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM). IAM Identity Center then issues the temporary AWS credentials used by Codex. The identity provider is not configured in Codex.

Prerequisites

  1. Add each pilot user to a dedicated group in the workforce identity system and provision that group to IAM Identity Center. Keep the assignment limited to the pilot.
  2. Choose an Amazon Bedrock Region and an OpenAI model available to the pilot identity, plus an inference profile if the selected API requires one. Check Sol, Terra, and Luna separately for the chosen account, Region, and inference path.
  3. Grant only the Amazon Bedrock model inference permissions used by Codex, any direct validation commands, and the selected observability destination.
  4. Prepare a non-production repository and name a rollback owner.

Configure

The pilot has three checks. First, sign in using the IAM Identity Center profile configured for the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and call Amazon Bedrock Runtime directly. Next, point Codex to the approved model. Finally, run a safe Codex task. The direct call isolates AWS access problems. The final step confirms the Codex configuration.

Step 1: Sign in and validate Amazon Bedrock Runtime access.

aws sso login --profile codex-bedrock
export AWS_PROFILE=codex-bedrock
aws bedrock-runtime converse
--model-id us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol
--messages '[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"Reply with OK"}]}]'
--region us-east-2

This command creates a short-lived AWS session and checks whether the profile can invoke the chosen model in the chosen Region. If it fails, resolve the profile, Region, model or inference-profile access, or IAM permissions before configuring Codex.

Step 2: Configure the Codex provider.

# ~/.codex/config.toml (or managed user configuration)
model_provider = "amazon-bedrock"
model = "openai.gpt-5.6-sol"

[model_providers.amazon-bedrock.aws]
profile = "codex-bedrock"
region = "us-east-2"

The model value is the Codex model ID. The profile selects the AWS IAM Identity Center session, and region tells Codex which AWS Region to use. Keep these settings in user-level or managed configuration so a repository cannot change the provider.

Verify the pilot and confirm rollback

Before adding users, make sure the pilot reaches the approved model, produces the expected records, and can be disabled cleanly.

  1. Identity: aws sts get-caller-identity returns the expected IAM Identity Center assumed-role session.
  2. Model access: The pilot profile invokes the approved model through the API and Region selected for the test.
  3. Codex access: The user completes a safe, read-only task in a non-production repository, and the expected request-path evidence is available.
  4. Evidence and rollback: The identity, invocation, audit, and optional telemetry records are present. Remove the configuration or IAM Identity Center assignment, handle any active session according to your procedure or wait for it to expire, and verify that a new invocation is denied.

Watch the Native AWS Access walkthrough

The walkthrough shows the complete pilot sequence: workforce sign-in, direct Amazon Bedrock Runtime validation, Codex provider configuration, and a safe test task.

Figure 2: Native AWS Access walkthrough covering workforce sign-in, Amazon Bedrock Runtime validation, Codex provider configuration, and a safe pilot task

Use the video to verify the order of the checks and the evidence to collect before adding more pilot users.

Run a two-user identity-isolation check

Two users are required to test identity isolation. A single user shows that sign-in works. A second user tests whether attribution remains distinct. Have two pilot users sign in separately and run the same harmless task. Their assumed-role sessions and audit records, and telemetry records if configured, should remain distinct.

The following diagram shows how separate pilot identities should produce separate AWS sessions, request evidence, and optional telemetry while using the same approved Codex and Amazon Bedrock path.

Figure 3: Use trusted identity enrollment for attribution. A local collector can add approved identity context only when it is deployed and configured as part of a managed enrollment process

Gateway paths for request-path controls

AgentCore Gateway is an option when you want AWS managed gateway infrastructure for centralized routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. If your organization already runs an LLM Gateway or wants to enforce controls in the request path, use that gateway instead. Validate the selected gateway before exposing it to pilot users.

LLM Gateway: Validate before a pilot

  1. Check that the gateway accepts the Codex request format.
  2. Use the sign-in or token flow defined by the gateway team.
  3. Before inviting pilot users, test model routing, monitoring, failure handling, and rollback.

Custom enterprise integration

A custom enterprise integration is the most involved form of the LLM Gateway pattern. Consider it only when Native AWS Access, AgentCore Gateway, and an existing gateway cannot meet a specific requirement. The result is another service to design, secure, test, support, and operate, so platform engineering and security need to own it from the start.

Observe, govern, and allocate cost

Codex OpenTelemetry, Amazon Bedrock service records, AWS identity records, and billing data answer different questions. Codex OpenTelemetry describes client activity. Amazon Bedrock service metrics and model invocation logs show service-side activity when enabled. AWS identity records and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) provide identity and billed-usage evidence. Correlate them for the path you deploy, and do not present token volume as a cost report.

Define what code, prompts, files, and tool output Codex might send through the selected model path. Exclude secrets and restricted data unless the organization has approved that data flow. Require developers to review and test generated changes before merge. Telemetry does not establish correctness or safety.

OpenTelemetry metrics from Codex

For observability, this post uses the ADOT collector configuration and CloudWatch dashboard from the repository’s monitoring and operations guidance. Deploy that configuration to each managed pilot device, then run a safe Codex task.

The repository provides the configuration files. Follow its deployment instructions to install the approved ADOT collector and configure its AWS authentication.

# ~/.codex/config.toml or managed user configuration
[otel]
environment = "pilot"
log_user_prompt = false
metrics_exporter = { "otlp-http" = { endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics", protocol = "binary" } }

Validate the repository path: run a safe Codex task and confirm that the expected operational metrics appear on the managed CloudWatch dashboard.

Telemetry plane Examples Attribution boundary
Codex OpenTelemetry metrics Token usage, turns, API requests, request duration, tool calls, session source. Per-user and team dashboard grouping only after the local collector adds validated identity attributes.
Amazon Bedrock service metrics Invocations, latency, input tokens, output tokens, client errors, server errors. Use the documented namespace, metric names, and dimensions for the selected Runtime, Mantle, or AgentCore path.
AWS identity evidence, model invocation logs, and CUR Assumed-role single sign-on (SSO) principal plus billed Bedrock line items. For Native IAM Identity Center access, CUR 2.0 with caller-identity allocation can expose the SSO principal. Gateway paths require gateway telemetry and spend records for end-user allocation.

Amazon CloudWatch dashboard and evidence

The Amazon CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights managed dashboard in the Guidance for Codex on AWS repository shows Codex operational metrics collected through ADOT. Use it to understand client activity, and use AWS identity, audit, and billing records separately when you need attribution or cost evidence.

Question Decision Evidence to keep
Who invoked the model? Use the AWS identity/audit source for the path you selected. Pilot identity record and request correlation, where available.
What did it cost? Use billing data for actual charge and label any inferred allocation clearly. CUR source, allocation method, and known uncertainty.
Can we stop unsafe or expensive behavior? Use alarms for detection. Use IAM and managed client controls for their respective access and action boundaries. Use gateway policy when request-path enforcement, such as hard budgets or rate limits, is required. Control test results and rollback procedure.

Watch the Codex OTel and CloudWatch walkthrough

The walkthrough shows how to query Codex OpenTelemetry metrics and confirm that the expected token and request data appears in Amazon CloudWatch.

Figure 4: Codex OpenTelemetry metrics shown in an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard

The example validates the aliased metric result in Amazon CloudWatch Query Studio and shows how the dashboard represents Codex client activity.

Standardize team behavior

After the infrastructure path is working, turn to the developer experience. Repository guidance, managed plugins, hooks, and approved MCP servers can make the rollout consistent without asking each team to assemble its own setup.

Plugins

Organization-owned plugins are a practical way to distribute shared skills, hooks, and approved MCP integrations. Give each plugin an owner and version, review changes before release, and publish it only through approved sources. Test updates with a pilot group and keep a documented removal path.

A plugin might include an MCP server configuration, but that does not make every bundled tool approved. Allow only the servers and tools the organization has reviewed, with user confirmation where it is needed.

Hooks

Hooks can be declared in hooks.json or directly in configuration. Keep the documented event casing, and deploy organization-owned policy commands through approved endpoint tooling.

[[hooks.PreToolUse]]
matcher = "^Bash$"

[[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]]
type = "command"
command = "/usr/local/bin/company-pre-tool-policy"
timeout = 30

Use PreToolUse, PostToolUse, or SessionStart where they solve a specific need. Before wider deployment, test allow, deny, timeout, and disconnected-endpoint behavior.

MCP

An MCP server connects Codex to another system, so each server creates a separate trust boundary. Limit access to the users and tools that need it, manage credentials through an approved OAuth or secrets process, and require confirmation for tools that change external systems. Keep MCP credentials out of the model-provider configuration.

Roll out in phases

The following diagram defines the scope and evidence required to advance from preparation through pilot, expansion, and organization-wide standardization.

Figure 5: Start with a controlled pilot, expand after validating the access path and operational evidence, and standardize the rollout after the operating model is proven

Administrator launch checklist

  1. Record the selected path, owning team, Region, and model in the change record.
  2. Limit the pilot identity to the required permissions, and document how issued credentials or tokens are handled.
  3. Run a non-production test that covers sign-in, model availability, and one safe Codex task.
  4. Check telemetry and audit output from the deployed version rather than assuming the example applies unchanged.
  5. Separate billed amounts from estimates in cost reporting.
  6. Exercise recovery: remove the configuration or assignment, handle any active session through the approved procedure or wait for it to expire, and verify that a new invocation is denied.

Clean up

When the pilot ends or access must be disabled, remove the rollout resources that are no longer required.

Remove the Codex model-provider and telemetry configuration from managed devices. Remove the IAM Identity Center pilot assignment or gateway access, revoke pilot tokens and secrets, and handle active sessions according to the approved procedure. Uninstall or disable the ADOT collector, and delete the pilot CloudWatch dashboard and alarms if they are not shared with another workload. Verify cleanup by confirming that a new model invocation is denied and that retired telemetry resources receive no new data.

Configuration boundaries

Keep model-provider, credential, and organization telemetry settings in user-level or managed configuration. Project-local .codex/config.toml is repository-scoped configuration: Review it as code, but do not treat it as an enterprise enforcement boundary. AGENTS.md is useful for durable repository guidance, such as test commands and coding conventions, but it is not an enforcement boundary either.

Setting type Recommended location Reason
Model provider, credentials, Region User-level or managed configuration These are endpoint and enterprise choices, not repository defaults.
OpenTelemetry exporter User-level or managed configuration Telemetry destination and data handling are organization controls.
Repository instructions AGENTS.md Carries durable guidance but is not an enforcement boundary.
Permission requirements Organization-managed requirements.toml Constrains supported security-sensitive client choices.

Conclusions and next steps

Codex can use Amazon Bedrock for inference with supported OpenAI models. Start with the least-complex access path that meets the requirement, prove the identity and model path with a small pilot, and add gateway or client controls only when they solve a specific need.

AgentCore Gateway provides an AWS managed gateway option for routing or Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Choose an LLM Gateway when a platform team wants to enforce controls in the request path. Build a custom integration only when the available paths cannot meet a documented requirement.

Expand in stages and use evidence from each stage to decide what comes next. The Guidance for Codex on AWS repository contains the maintained configurations and validation procedures used in this post.

About the authors

translation.html:
开发者越来越多地将 Codex 与 Amazon Bedrock 配合使用，以探索不熟悉的代码、进行修改并处理重复性的工程工作。对于平台团队来说，挑战在于如何提供这些工具，同时避免再搭建一套模型访问、身份和运维体系。

Codex 可以通过 Amazon Bedrock 使用受支持的 OpenAI 模型进行推理。本文将展示如何将这条路径融入组织现有的 AWS 身份、AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）、区域和可观测性实践。Codex 仍在开发者工作站上运行。主要的设计选择在于，它的模型请求如何到达 Amazon Bedrock，以及组织在何处实施策略和运维控制。

我们从一个遵循最小权限原则的小规模试点开始，逐步完成扩大访问范围前的重要检查。示例使用 GPT-5.6 Sol。开始试点前，请查阅按 AWS 区域划分的 Amazon Bedrock 支持模型，确认 Sol、Terra 或 Luna 在你计划使用的 AWS 区域和推理路径中可用。

推荐的默认方案：使用 Native AWS Access 启动一个遵循最小权限原则的小规模试点。如果你希望使用 AWS 托管的网关基础设施进行路由或应用 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails，请选择 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能 AgentCore Gateway。如果平台团队希望在请求路径中强制实施控制，请选择 LLM Gateway。自定义集成是 LLM Gateway 模式的进阶形式，不是快速入门方案。

这些示例来自开源的 Guidance for Codex on AWS 仓库。该仓库包含 Native AWS Access、AgentCore Gateway、在 ECS 上运行 LiteLLM、Portkey、AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry（ADOT）的快速入门指南，以及本文后面使用的 Amazon CloudWatch 配置。请选择与你的架构匹配的快速入门指南，将其用于试点，并根据你的环境进行调整。

选择推广路径

身份验证只是企业推广的一部分。需要确定谁可以使用该服务，以及批准使用哪些模型和区域。还需要明确配置存放在哪里、收集哪些遥测数据、如何分摊用量，以及允许使用哪些技能或 Model Context Protocol（MCP）服务器。下表将这些需求对应到访问路径和负责团队。

选择能够提供当前所需控制的访问路径。能够满足要求的最直接路径，通常运维开销也最低。

决策规则

  1. 当 AWS 身份和 IAM 控制足以满足试点需求时，Native AWS Access 通常是起点。
  2. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 是一个可使用任意框架或模型，大规模构建、连接和优化智能体的平台。在该平台中，AgentCore Gateway 适合希望使用 AWS 托管的网关基础设施来实现路由、Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 或相关控制的团队。
  3. 大语言模型（LLM）网关适合已经在运营网关，或希望在请求路径中强制实施控制的组织。构建自定义网关是这一选项的进阶形式。

下图比较了三种推广路径中身份、路由、策略、遥测以及运维责任各自所处的位置。

图 1：在每种场景中，Codex 都在开发者工作站上运行。Native AWS Access 使用 AWS IAM Identity Center；配置后的 AgentCore Gateway 可以应用托管路由和 Guardrails；配置后的 LLM Gateway 可以应用请求路径控制

Native AWS Access

如果 Native AWS Access 适合该试点，仓库中的 Native AWS Access 快速入门指南提供了完整流程和配套文件。下面的简要演练重点介绍操作顺序和最重要的检查。

使用员工身份提供商登录

员工继续通过他们已经使用的身份提供商登录。在此示例中，Okta 通过安全断言标记语言（SAML）处理身份验证，并通过跨域身份管理系统（SCIM）将用户和组预配到 IAM Identity Center。随后，IAM Identity Center 签发供 Codex 使用的临时 AWS 凭证。身份提供商不在 Codex 中配置。

前提条件

  1. 将每位试点用户添加到员工身份系统中的专用组，并将该组预配到 IAM Identity Center。将分配范围限制在试点内。
  2. 选择试点身份可以使用的 Amazon Bedrock 区域和 OpenAI 模型；如果所选 API 需要，还应选择推理配置文件。针对所选账户、区域和推理路径，分别检查 Sol、Terra 和 Luna。
  3. 仅授予 Codex、任何直接验证命令以及所选可观测性目标所使用的 Amazon Bedrock 模型推理权限。
  4. 准备一个非生产仓库，并指定回滚负责人。

配置

试点包含三项检查。首先，使用为 AWS Command Line Interface（AWS CLI）配置的 IAM Identity Center 配置文件登录，并直接调用 Amazon Bedrock Runtime。然后，将 Codex 指向获批模型。最后，运行一个安全的 Codex 任务。直接调用有助于单独排查 AWS 访问问题。最后一步用于确认 Codex 配置。

步骤 1：登录并验证 Amazon Bedrock Runtime 访问权限。

aws sso login --profile codex-bedrock
export AWS_PROFILE=codex-bedrock
aws bedrock-runtime converse
--model-id us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol
--messages '[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"Reply with OK"}]}]'
--region us-east-2

此命令会创建一个短期 AWS 会话，并检查该配置文件是否可以在所选区域中调用所选模型。如果失败，请先解决配置文件、区域、模型或推理配置文件访问权限，或 IAM 权限方面的问题，再配置 Codex。

步骤 2：配置 Codex 提供商。

# ~/.codex/config.toml (or managed user configuration)
model_provider = "amazon-bedrock"
model = "openai.gpt-5.6-sol"

[model_providers.amazon-bedrock.aws]
profile = "codex-bedrock"
region = "us-east-2"

model 的值是 Codex 模型 ID。profile 用于选择 AWS IAM Identity Center 会话，region 告知 Codex 使用哪个 AWS 区域。将这些设置保存在用户级或托管配置中，以使仓库无法更改提供商。

验证试点并确认回滚

在添加用户前，确保试点能够访问获批模型、生成预期记录，并且能够彻底停用。

  1. 身份：aws sts get-caller-identity 返回预期的 IAM Identity Center 代入角色会话。
  2. 模型访问：试点配置文件通过为测试选定的 API 和区域调用获批模型。
  3. Codex 访问：用户在非生产仓库中完成一个安全的只读任务，并且能够获取预期的请求路径证据。
  4. 证据与回滚：身份、调用、审计以及可选的遥测记录均已存在。移除配置或 IAM Identity Center 分配，按照既定流程处理任何活动会话，或等待其过期，并验证新的调用会被拒绝。

观看 Native AWS Access 操作演练

该演练展示了完整的试点流程：员工登录、直接验证 Amazon Bedrock Runtime、配置 Codex 提供商，以及执行安全的测试任务。

图 2：Native AWS Access 操作演练，涵盖员工登录、Amazon Bedrock Runtime 验证、Codex 提供商配置和安全的试点任务

使用该视频核实检查顺序，以及在添加更多试点用户前需要收集的证据。

执行双用户身份隔离检查

测试身份隔离需要两名用户。单个用户可以证明登录有效。第二名用户用于测试归属信息是否保持独立。让两名试点用户分别登录并运行同一个无害任务。他们的代入角色会话和审计记录，以及在已配置情况下的遥测记录，应保持彼此独立。

下图展示了不同的试点身份在使用相同的获批 Codex 和 Amazon Bedrock 路径时，应如何产生独立的 AWS 会话、请求证据以及可选的遥测数据。

图 3：使用可信的身份注册来确定归属。只有当本地收集器作为受管注册流程的一部分进行部署和配置时，它才能添加获批的身份上下文

用于请求路径控制的网关路径

如果你希望使用 AWS 托管的网关基础设施进行集中路由或应用 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails，AgentCore Gateway 是一个选项。如果你的组织已经运行 LLM Gateway，或希望在请求路径中强制实施控制，则使用该网关。在向试点用户开放之前，先验证所选网关。

LLM Gateway：试点前先验证

  1. 检查网关是否接受 Codex 请求格式。
  2. 使用网关团队定义的登录或令牌流程。
  3. 在邀请试点用户之前，测试模型路由、监控、故障处理和回滚。

自定义企业集成

自定义企业集成是 LLM Gateway 模式中最复杂的形式。只有当 Native AWS Access、AgentCore Gateway 和现有网关都无法满足某项具体要求时，才考虑它。这会带来另一项需要设计、保护、测试、支持和运营的服务，因此平台工程和安全团队需要从一开始就负责。

观测、治理与成本分摊

Codex OpenTelemetry、Amazon Bedrock 服务记录、AWS 身份记录和计费数据分别回答不同的问题。Codex OpenTelemetry 描述客户端活动。Amazon Bedrock 服务指标和模型调用日志在启用后显示服务端活动。AWS 身份记录和 AWS Cost and Usage Report（CUR）提供身份和已计费用量的证据。针对你部署的路径关联这些数据，不要将 token 数量当作成本报告。

明确 Codex 可能通过所选模型路径发送哪些代码、提示词、文件和工具输出。除非组织已批准相应数据流，否则应排除机密信息和受限数据。要求开发者在合并前审查并测试生成的更改。遥测数据无法证明正确性或安全性。

来自 Codex 的 OpenTelemetry 指标

在可观测性方面，本文使用仓库监控与运维指南中的 ADOT 收集器配置和 CloudWatch 仪表板。将该配置部署到每台受管试点设备，然后运行一个安全的 Codex 任务。

仓库提供了配置文件。按照其中的部署说明安装获批的 ADOT 收集器，并配置其 AWS 身份验证。

# ~/.codex/config.toml or managed user configuration
[otel]
environment = "pilot"
log_user_prompt = false
metrics_exporter = { "otlp-http" = { endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics", protocol = "binary" } }

验证仓库提供的路径：运行一个安全的 Codex 任务，并确认预期的运维指标出现在受管 CloudWatch 仪表板上。

遥测平面 示例 归属边界
Codex OpenTelemetry 指标 Token 用量、轮次、API 请求、请求时长、工具调用、会话来源。 只有在本地收集器添加经过验证的身份属性后，才能在仪表板中按用户和团队分组。
Amazon Bedrock 服务指标 调用次数、延迟、输入 token 数、输出 token 数、客户端错误、服务器错误。 使用所选 Runtime、Mantle 或 AgentCore 路径文档中规定的命名空间、指标名称和维度。
AWS 身份证据、模型调用日志和 CUR 代入角色的单点登录（SSO）主体，以及已计费的 Bedrock 明细项目。 对于原生 IAM Identity Center 访问，启用调用者身份分摊的 CUR 2.0 可以显示 SSO 主体。网关路径需要借助网关遥测数据和支出记录，将用量或成本分摊到最终用户。

Amazon CloudWatch 仪表板与证据

Guidance for Codex on AWS 仓库中的 Amazon CloudWatch Coding Agent Insights 托管仪表板展示了通过 ADOT 收集的 Codex 运维指标。使用它来了解客户端活动；当你需要归属或成本证据时，应另行使用 AWS 身份、审计和计费记录。

问题 决策 应保留的证据
谁调用了模型？ 使用所选路径对应的 AWS 身份或审计数据源。 试点身份记录，以及可用时的请求关联信息。
花费了多少？ 使用计费数据确定实际费用，并清楚标注任何推算的分摊结果。 CUR 数据源、分摊方法和已知不确定性。
我们能否阻止不安全或昂贵的行为？ 使用告警进行检测。使用 IAM 和受管客户端控制，分别约束其对应的访问和操作边界。当需要强制实施硬性预算或速率限制等请求路径控制时，使用网关策略。 控制措施测试结果和回滚流程。

规范团队行为

基础设施路径正常运行后，接下来关注开发者体验。仓库指南、受管插件、钩子和获批的 MCP 服务器可以让推广保持一致，无需每个团队自行组装配置。

插件

组织自有插件是分发共享技能、钩子和获批 MCP 集成的一种实用方式。为每个插件指定负责人和版本，在发布前审查更改，并且仅通过获批来源发布。先在试点组中测试更新，并保留有文档说明的移除路径。

插件可能包含 MCP 服务器配置，但这并不意味着其中捆绑的每个工具都已获批。仅允许组织已审查的服务器和工具，并在需要时要求用户确认。

钩子

钩子可以在 hooks.json 中声明，也可以直接在配置中声明。保持文档规定的事件名称大小写，并通过获批的终端管理工具部署组织自有的策略命令。

[[hooks.PreToolUse]]
matcher = "^Bash$"

[[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]]
type = "command"
command = "/usr/local/bin/company-pre-tool-policy"
timeout = 30

在能够满足具体需求时，使用 PreToolUse、PostToolUse 或 SessionStart。在扩大部署前，测试允许、拒绝、超时以及终端断开连接时的行为。

MCP

MCP 服务器将 Codex 连接到另一个系统，因此每个服务器都会形成一个独立的信任边界。将访问权限限制为确有需要的用户和工具，通过获批的 OAuth 或机密管理流程管理凭证，并要求对会更改外部系统的工具进行确认。不要将 MCP 凭证放入模型提供商配置中。

下图定义了从准备到试点、扩大范围，再到全组织标准化，各阶段推进所需的范围和证据。

图 5：从受控试点开始，在验证访问路径和运维证据后扩大范围，并在运营模式得到验证后将推广标准化

管理员启动检查清单

  1. 在变更记录中记下所选路径、负责团队、区域和模型。
  2. 将试点身份限制在必需权限内，并记录如何处理已签发的凭证或令牌。
  3. 执行一次非生产测试，涵盖登录、模型可用性和一个安全的 Codex 任务。
  4. 检查已部署版本的遥测和审计输出，不要假定示例可以原样适用。
  5. 在成本报告中区分已计费金额与估算值。
  6. 演练恢复流程：移除配置或分配，按照获批流程处理任何活动会话，或等待其过期，并验证新的调用会被拒绝。

清理

当试点结束或必须停用访问时，移除不再需要的推广资源。

从受管设备中移除 Codex 模型提供商和遥测配置。移除 IAM Identity Center 试点分配或网关访问权限，撤销试点令牌和机密，并按照获批流程处理活动会话。卸载或禁用 ADOT 收集器；如果试点 CloudWatch 仪表板和告警未与其他工作负载共享，也将其删除。通过确认新的模型调用会被拒绝，以及已停用的遥测资源不再接收新数据，来验证清理结果。

配置边界

将模型提供商、凭证和组织遥测设置保存在用户级或托管配置中。项目本地的 .codex/config.toml 是仓库范围的配置：应像代码一样审查它，但不要将其视为企业级强制控制边界。AGENTS.md 适合承载测试命令和编码约定等长期有效的仓库指南，但它同样不是强制控制边界。

设置类型 推荐位置 原因
模型提供商、凭证、区域 用户级或托管配置 这些是终端和企业层面的选择，不是仓库默认值。
OpenTelemetry 导出器 用户级或托管配置 遥测目标和数据处理属于组织控制事项。
仓库指令 AGENTS.md 承载长期有效的指南，但不是强制控制边界。
权限要求 由组织管理的 requirements.toml 约束受支持且涉及安全的客户端选项。

结论与后续步骤

Codex 可以通过 Amazon Bedrock 使用受支持的 OpenAI 模型进行推理。从满足要求且复杂度最低的访问路径开始，通过小规模试点验证身份和模型路径，并且仅在能够解决具体需求时添加网关或客户端控制。

AgentCore Gateway 提供 AWS 托管的网关选项，用于路由或应用 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails。当平台团队希望在请求路径中强制实施控制时，选择 LLM Gateway。只有在现有路径无法满足已记录的要求时，才构建自定义集成。

分阶段扩大范围，并使用每个阶段的证据决定下一步。Guidance for Codex on AWS 仓库包含本文使用且持续维护的配置和验证流程。
